transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-28 16:00 UTC
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Kim (Redwood SE), Ana Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Connor Lee (Redwood Product), Maya Torres (Citrine Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Citrine Infra), Ravi Das (Citrine Security), Elena Park (Citrine PM), Sean (data)

Summary: final-week POC sync to confirm go/no-go checklist, routing matrix for canary and A/B splits, monitoring/alerting runbooks, and security sign-offs. Agreed next steps and owners.

Topics: go-live decision criteria, traffic steering matrix, fallback models, latency soak, observability dashboards, compliance sign-off, roll-back plan.

[00:00] Samir: ok hey everyone thanks for joining, uh we'll run through the final checklist today and make sure the routing matrix and runbooks are nailed down.
[00:18] Maya: thanks, yeah we've got exec time next week so need to lock decisions.
[00:23] Jules: I have the canary gating doc up, and I pulled the telemetry from the last 48 hours so we can set thresholds.
[00:33] Liam: quick note, infra will only allow a 15% pre-roll burst on day one; anything above needs additional quota.
[00:40] Samir: noted. we'll design the routing to respect that. quick intro: this POC used a hosted Redwood inference endpoint with a dedicated fallback to local private nodes — ppl might call that Redwood Dedicated vs Redwood Private but there was a tiny mislabel in the doc earlier.
[00:58] Elena: slight correction, legal asked about KMS - is that customer-managed?
[01:05] Samir: yes, for Private we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM. we'll add the KMS diagram to the runbook.

--- Automatic summary / auto-generated highlights (may be noisy) ---
[01:20] AutoSummary: latency target 120-180ms p95, canary success = no more than 1.5x error rate relative to baseline, memory leakage observed in pod group B during long-run, need to re-check KV cache behavior (transcribed as KV cash in raw log).

[02:02] Jules: ok on canary thresholds we propose p95 latency < 180ms, error rate < 1.5x baseline, and model-quality checks — we'll use the existing golden prompt set that Maya shared.
[02:18] Maya: that works, but two quality checks: hallucination score and slot-filling accuracy. can we automate a shortlist so we don't do thousands manually?
[02:28] Jules: yes we run lightweight rerank and a small evaluator that samples 200 requests per hour during canary. that will trigger rollback if quality drops more than the threshold.

[03:10] Liam: about routing matrix, so step one is 0.5% -> 5% -> 15% over 3 windows, correct?
[03:18] Samir: correct. propose 2-hour windows for the first two ramps and a 6-hour observation for the final 15% stage. with automatic rollback on telemetry WRT error/latency/quality.
[03:30] Elena: what's the rollback path? full revert to previous model or degrade to smaller single-region model?
[03:36] Jules: fallback plan is layered: first fallback to the compatible quantized variant, e.g. redwood-3b-q (note: earlier doc used redwood-3b-quant but the runtime calls it redwood-3b-q), if issues persist then route to the baseline smaller model hosted in a different region.
[03:55] Sean (speaker listed as Guest): uh question - will the A/B test be at the request route level or session level?
[04:01] Samir: good q, for Citrine we recommend request-level routing so that individual prompts can be compared; session-level has stickiness complexity.

[04:30] Ravi: security question - audit logs and retention. we need three months retention with immutable logs for compliance; can we ensure that?
[04:39] Samir: yes, Redwood Console can export audit logs to your S3 with immutability policy; we'll add the policy snippet to the runbook.
[04:47] Ravi: and SSO? we require SAML 2.0 and SCIM for provisioning.
[04:52] Ana: we support SAML and SCIM; I'll follow up with the SSO guide and a sample metadata file.

[05:10] Jules: a note from the latency soak yesterday — one of the GPU nodes in the dedicated pool hit a high swap churn when sequence length jumped; looks like the kernel selection triggered a slower path. not blocking but we should avoid long 4096-token requests during initial rollout.
[05:30] Maya: we can cap max tokens to 1024 for the first two weeks.
[05:35] Samir: we'll put that into traffic steering rules.

[06:00] Connor: monitoring — what dashboards should we hand over?
[06:05] Jules: primary dashboard: p95/p99 latency per route, error rate, model-quality score (auto eval fail rate), kv-cache hit ratio, and per-region capacity utilization. secondary: token cost burn rate and per-route unit cost.
[06:20] Elena: can you add an alert when cost burn is 20% above expected run-rate? we want early visibility.
[06:26] Samir: yes, we can wire a cost anomaly alert in Redwood Console.

[07:00] [transcript noise: brief crosstalk]
[07:12] Maya: about the routing matrix spreadsheet — I uploaded a draft, check tab 'routing-matrix-v3' — make sure weight columns match.
[07:23] Jules: found a mismatch in region aliasing where us-east-1 was mapped twice, I'll patch and send back.

[08:00] Samir: let's walk the go/no-go checklist quickly:
[08:06] - Security sign-off on KMS/SAML? (Ravi)
[08:10] - Observability dashboard and alerts validated? (Citrine + Redwood)
[08:13] - Latency soak completed successfully? (Jules)
[08:16] - Runbook and rollback steps published? (Samir)
[08:19] - Quota approved for 15% ramp? (Liam)

[08:25] Ravi: pending KMS diagram and audit retention snippet, I can't sign off until I see the immutability configuration.
[08:33] Liam: quota request is approved up to 15% but anything above requires cloud SP support.
[08:38] Maya: quality threshold confirm from our side, we need the golden set automation in place.

[09:00] Jules: on soak scheduling — propose to run the 2-hour latency soak tomorrow at 02:00 UTC using the prod-like payload generator. will hit a 90/10 mix of short->long prompts.
[09:10] Maya: that works. I'll make sure the golden prompts are mounted.

[09:35] Samir: regarding traffic steering rules, the routing matrix will be explicit: route_id, region_preference, percent_traffic, fallback_order, max_tokens_limit, canary_window_hours, success_criteria. we'll deliver a CSV that you can drop into the Redwood Console import.
[09:56] Elena: you mentioned import — is the console import idempotent? we need to ensure it doesn't duplicate rules.
[10:03] Ana: import is idempotent if route_id matches; we'll validate against your existing route_ids.

[10:30] [12:15] (transcription glitch — speaker attribution uncertain)
[10:40] Jules: small gotcha: when migrating, the KV cache keys differ across model variants; so early ramp could see cache misses and cause a transient 5-10% latency bump. that's expected and included in our canary tolerances.
[11:00] Maya: fine but we want it documented.

[11:20] Samir: runbook outline: pre-flight check, stepwise ramp commands, monitoring checkpoints, automatic rollback triggers, manual abort steps, and post-mortem checklist. we'll attach runbook to the ticket.
[11:32] Elena: include contact matrix with phone numbers and on-call rotations.
[11:36] Samir: yes, will include on-call.

[12:00] Liam: about A/B vs canary — if we do A/B for a subset of requests we must make sure experiment logging includes request_id and variant_id, otherwise our analytics will be impossible.
[12:12] Jules: we'll add variant metadata to the request headers and ensure that logs forward to your analytics pipeline.

[13:00] Ravi: compliance — do you have a SOC2 report we can review?
[13:05] Samir: yes, will share the redacted SOC2 and ISO docs; note sometimes filenames have Redwood spelled as Redwod in the internal bucket (lol transcription), but the docs are current.

[13:30] Maya: pricing note — we want rough cost delta if we use fallback quantized model vs baseline; can you provide a per-100k-token estimate?
[13:38] Samir: we'll add a cost table to the runbook, quick ballpark: quantized variant ~30% cheaper per-token; we'll produce exact numbers after the soak run.

[14:05] Jules: final risk table items: cross-region latency, KV cache miss bump, quota limits, golden-set regression risk. each has mitigation in runbook.

[14:30] [brief pause / typing sounds]
[14:36] Samir: ok wrap-up — let's go round-robin with commitments. Samir first.
[14:40] Samir: I'll send finalized runbook + routing matrix by EOD 2026-03-29 and the SOC2/ISO links today.
[14:48] Jules: I'll run the latency soak 2026-03-31 and share results; also patch the region aliasing in the spreadsheet.
[14:55] Ana: I'll send SSO/SCIM sample metadata and the console import instructions.
[15:02] Maya: Citrine will confirm canary success criteria and golden prompt set by 2026-03-30.
[15:07] Liam: I'll confirm quota with cloud SP and ensure the infra playbooks are ready.
[15:12] Ravi: I'll review KMS and audit log immutability and sign off by 2026-04-02.

[15:30] Elena: schedule wise, when would you propose the actual live cutover?
[15:36] Samir: earliest safe window is 2026-04-06 if all sign-offs complete. we prefer a low-traffic weekend window.
[15:44] Elena: sounds good, we'll tentatively pencil that in.

[16:00] Samir: any blockers?
[16:02] Maya: just KMS diagram and automated golden-check.
[16:05] Samir: we'll prioritize those.

Recap / Next Steps:
- Samir: runbook + routing matrix + SOC2 links (due 2026-03-29)
- Jules: latency soak and spreadsheet fixes (due 2026-03-31)
- Maya: confirm canary success criteria and golden prompts (due 2026-03-30)
- Ravi: security sign-off on audit retention and KMS (due 2026-04-02)

End of meeting.

Links/References mentioned: routing-matrix-v3.csv (uploaded by customer), golden-prompts-v2.json (customer share), Redwood Console import guide (redwood.com/docs/console/import)

Transcript notes: imperfect speaker attribution in a couple places, occasional ASR mis-heard tokens (KV cash instead of KV cache), proper nouns sometimes garbled.
